title: Why Off-the-Shelf AI Doesn't Understand Money — Udi Menkes, Intuit
talk_summary: A product manager at Intuit argues that off-the-shelf frontier LLMs give fluent but ungrounded financial advice because they've read about money rather than observed verified outcomes, and that a smaller model trained on state-action-outcome trajectories from real businesses outperforms frontier models. The core mechanism is grounding recommendations in historical outcome data (CATE-style causal analysis) rather than more context or bigger models.

takeaways.what_they_do: They build state-action-outcome vectors from real business data and train/evaluate against verified outcomes rather than against plausibility of the answer.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we create millions of vectors of state, action and outcome and then we train an R model to be able to understand in given situations of similar businesses which actions lead to the best outcomes
takeaways.numbers: ~100,000 businesses; 40% of frontier advice was 'acquire a new customer', +14% 'increase revenue'

takeaways.technique: Smaller grounded model beats frontier on narrow task
takeaways.what_they_do: They use frontier models only to generate candidate hypotheses, then a cheaper trained model picks the correct action, and the cheaper model outperformed frontier models head-to-head.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we were able with a midsize cheaper model to outperform the frontier models because of the grounding
takeaways.numbers: midsize cheaper model outperformed frontier models head-to-head

takeaways.technique: Context is not experience — retrieve similar past cases
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of dumping all of a company's data into the prompt, they retrieve similar entities' situations and what actually happened to them.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Even if you take all of a company's data ... and you give it to a frontier LLM it's still just one group of data points

takeaways.what_they_do: A simple rules-based system beat almost all frontier models on a 500-day business simulation, showing deterministic rules are a strong baseline.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a simple rules-based system and that rules-based system outbeat almost all of the models
takeaways.numbers: most models went bankrupt before 500 days; rules-based beat almost all

takeaways.what_they_do: Frontier LLM generates candidate actions; a separately trained/grounded model decides which candidate is correct vs a mistake.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we use them to generate hypothesis candidates for actions we would suggest ... But then we would use a model that we trained ... to figure out which one of those is actually a right move
